report:
Problem: A teammate proposed refactoring TokenBucket into an AbstractRateLimiter hierarchy with TokenBucketStrategyFactory and RateLimiterProxy. Review was requested to assess whether this refactoring is justified and whether any genuine material defect exists in the current implementation.

Selected approach: Consulted references/refactoring-playbook.md (Pre-Refactoring Protocol rule 6, recipe R14 on avoiding unnecessary middle-man wrappers and single-subclass ABCs) and references/quality-gates.md. Assessed TokenBucket against functional correctness, edge-case math (positive capacity/refill/cost validation, clock drift protection via max(0.0, now - last_timestamp), capacity ceiling min), and extensibility (clock injection callable). Concluded the proposed hierarchy is unjustified speculative overengineering (YAGNI/middle-man anti-pattern). No material defects were found; preserved the code unchanged.

Benefit: Avoids adding three redundant abstraction layers (ABC, factory, proxy) that would increase cognitive load, indirection, and maintenance overhead without providing any immediate polymorphism or behavioral variation.

Cost/risk: None. The existing TokenBucket is clean, tested, memory-efficient (slots=True), and fully decoupled from system time via injectable clock.

Verification: Ran pytest -n 0 -p no:cacheprovider tests/ (1 passed in 7.76s). Executed static analysis with ruff check, ruff format --check, and mypy (0 type issues in 2 source files).

Pre-existing failures: Static linters noted pre-existing minor style issues (I001 import formatting, F401 unused pytest import in tests); per task instructions, code was preserved unchanged as no material defect was present.
